`pipeshub login --no-wait`: give the user the link and code, and finish with
`pipeshub login --wait`. Then run `pipeshub mcp install --client claude-code`
(or `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`, `claude-desktop`) and restart the client.
Otherwise they mint a personal access
token in Workspace → Developer settings. They export it in their shell profile
as `PIPESHUB_MCP_TOKEN` (never into chat) and restart the agent. With the
PipesHub Claude Code plugin, run `/pipeshub:setup` to check it. Otherwise:
findings.message: Code accesses credential files (SSH keys, AWS credentials, etc.). This could indicate credential theft attempts.
findings.remediation: Remove references to credential paths. Use environment variables or secrets managers. For docs, use placeholder paths (e.g., /path/to/config). Never load .env or token files in production code paths.

findings.code_snippet:
- IDE clients (Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini): create an OAuth app and follow
     the client's setup page. Redirect URIs are listed at
     https://docs.pipeshub.com/mcp/overview.md
   - Scripts and the stdio bridge: a personal access token as
     `Authorization: Bearer`.
   - **Never** `client_credentials` — that grant has no `userId`, so everyone
     sees everything the client can see.

and chat both 500 until that LLM exists. Slack/Drive need OAuth; for a
demo upload files to the Knowledge Base (no mount) or Local FS with a
bind-mount.
